laravel.version: 11.x|12.x|13.x (illuminate/* components, package monorepo not full app)

stack_summary.notes: Package monorepo — audit adapted to library packages under packages/*; unit-only policy from AGENTS.md respected (no Feature-test recommendations).

findings.title: HTTP controllers lack Illuminate Request/Response bridge

locations.snippet: Controllers map real Illuminate requests into this shape at the adapter edge.

findings.current_state: Routes are registered as CapabilityController@list (etc.) onto the Illuminate router, but actions accept only HttpRequestContext and return package HttpResponse DTOs. There is no fromRequest/toResponse adapter, no Responsable implementation, and no factory that copies Sanctum user, headers, JSON body, or credential abilities into HttpRequestContext.
findings.recommended_state: Ship an edge adapter (e.g. HttpRequestContext::fromIlluminate(Request) + HttpResponse implementing Responsable or toIlluminate()) and either invokable controllers that take Request or a thin Laravel controller that maps in/out. Ensure credential/user/authKind come from middleware-resolved auth, never client claims.
findings.rationale: Without a bridge, container resolution builds a default unauthenticated HttpRequestContext (all constructor defaults), so catalog/invoke either always 401 or never see the real actor. Returning a non-Response DTO also breaks the HTTP kernel. This is a concrete prod-break for the single HTTP/CLI API (D-009) despite extensive unit coverage of pure controllers.
findings.implementation_hint: Add packages/laravel-capabilities/src/Http/IlluminateHttpBridge.php; bind controllers that accept Request, map to HttpRequestContext (user, token abilities → credential, headers, jsonBody, authKind), call existing methods, return response()->json($http->body, $http->status)->withHeaders($http->headers). Unit-test the mapper with array fixtures (still no Feature suite).

findings.title: AuthController issues placeholder tokens from client body
findings.current_state: AuthController is a contract stub: token() echoes client-supplied access_token or 'issued-by-host', device() returns fixed placeholders, oauthCallback() echoes query code. These routes are registered in RouteTable when HTTP is enabled (default middleware includes auth:sanctum).
findings.recommended_state: Either do not register auth routes until a real host AuthIssuer is bound, or implement host-delegated issuance behind explicit interfaces (Sanctum/Passport/OAuth device flow) and never accept client-supplied access_token. Fail closed with 501/not_configured when unbound.
findings.rationale: Registering stub token endpoints on the product capability API creates a footgun: if middleware is relaxed for CLI bootstrap, clients can obtain a fake bearer string that may confuse downstream gateways. Even with Sanctum, oauth/device routes are not a safe chicken-egg design for CLI login.
findings.implementation_hint: Introduce AuthTokenIssuer interface; AuthController returns not_found unless bound. Split middleware: auth flows without auth:sanctum, catalog/invoke with it. Mirror shape used by CLI internal/auth package expectations.

findings.title: Registry defaults to allow-all when capability has no authorize()
findings.current_state: stageAuthorize uses the capability's authorize callable when present; otherwise it calls the injected Authorizer. Construction defaults to StubAuthorizer::allow(). makeRegistry / ServiceProvider never bind a production Authorizer or force per-capability authorize.
findings.recommended_state: Fail closed: default StubAuthorizer::deny() (or a DenyUnlessAuthorizeCallable authorizer) for mutating capabilities without authorize; require explicit withAuthorizer / host GateAuthorizer in ContainerBindings plan; document that authorize() is mandatory for non-readOnly definitions.
findings.rationale: Governance is part of every surface (AGENTS.md). A host that registers capabilities with only run() gets silent allow for any authenticated actor on HTTP/agent/MCP/job. That is fail-open relative to package security claims.
findings.implementation_hint: Change default to StubAuthorizer::deny(); in CapabilityDefinitionBuilder::register, reject mutating defs without authorize; add unit test that registry from makeRegistry denies when authorize missing.

findings.title: Messaging provider never binds services; webhook uses FakeQueue
findings.current_state: MessagingServiceProvider only merges config and optionally loads routes. It never registers MessagingBindings singletons. TelegramWebhookController defaults queue to FakeQueue (in-memory list). MessagingBindings::build always constructs FakeTelegramBotClient + FakeQueue even as the pure 'production plan' path.
findings.recommended_state: register() should bind MessagingConfig from config repository, a real LaravelQueue adapter implementing UpdateQueue, real TelegramBotClient (HTTP), durable IdentityLinker/ThreadStore, and ProcessTelegramUpdate. Webhook must not default to FakeQueue outside testing.
findings.rationale: With telegram enabled (config default env CAPABILITIES_TELEGRAM true), routes accept webhooks, verify secrets, and 'queue' updates into a process-local FakeQueue that no worker drains. Outbound bot calls would also be fakes if bindings were used as-is. This is a production-break for the messaging surface.
findings.implementation_hint: Add Support/LaravelUpdateQueue using Bus::dispatch(ProcessTelegramUpdateJob); bind in MessagingServiceProvider::register from MessagingBindings::production($app); inject Fake* only when app.env is testing or via config driver=fake.

findings.title: DatabaseApprovalStore generates sequential process-local IDs
findings.current_state: When put() omits id, DatabaseApprovalStore assigns approval-{n} from an in-memory sequence counter. QueryTableGateway already generates cryptographically random hex IDs when id is absent at insert time, but the store always pre-assigns sequential ids first.
findings.recommended_state: Use random/UUID ids for durable approvals (delegate to gateway or bin2hex(random_bytes(16)) / Str::ulid()). Keep sequential ids only in InMemoryApprovalStore for unit readability.
findings.rationale: Multi-worker PHP-FPM/queue processes each restart sequence at 1 → primary-key collisions or overwrites. Predictable approval IDs also weaken URL/callback unguessability if accept routes leak.
findings.implementation_hint: In DatabaseApprovalStore::put, omit id and let QueryTableGateway::resolveId mint random ids, or call random_bytes like IdempotencyKey. Add unit test for uniqueness across two store instances.

findings.title: Messaging identity and threads are memory-only with empty migrations

locations.snippet:
/** @var array<string, array{user_id: string, tenant_id: string|null, telegram_user_id: string}> */
    private array $links = [];
Conversation thread persistence (in-memory for unit tests; swap driver in production).

findings.current_state: IdentityLinker and ThreadStore hold links/codes/history in private arrays. database/migrations is published but empty. No production store implementation is registered.
findings.recommended_state: Add durable drivers (DB tables for identity links, link codes, threads) behind the same interfaces; publish real migrations; bind database drivers when not testing. Keep in-memory implementations for unit tests only.
findings.rationale: Multi-process webhooks lose link state between requests; link codes issued on one worker are invisible to another. Conversation continuity and identity (MSG pipeline resolve_identity) cannot work under normal Laravel deploy topology.
findings.implementation_hint: Migrations for messaging_identity_links / messaging_link_codes / messaging_threads; DatabaseIdentityLinker implementing ConversationIdentity; unit-test against ArrayTableGateway pattern from core package.

findings.title: Approval claimLease is check-then-act without lease condition
findings.current_state: claimLease reads the row, evaluates execution_lease_until in PHP, then updateWhere only on id+status. Two concurrent accept/resume workers can both pass the lease check before either writes.
findings.recommended_state: Atomic claim: single UPDATE ... WHERE id=? AND status=? AND (execution_lease_until IS NULL OR execution_lease_until < ?) and require affected rows = 1. Extend TableGateway if needed for SQL-side predicates.
findings.rationale: D-006 requires exactly-once execution and crash recovery. compareAndUpdate helps status races, but lease claiming remains TOCTOU under concurrency — dual run() of the same approved capability is possible.
findings.implementation_hint: Add TableGateway::updateWhereExpr or claimLease SQL on QueryTableGateway; unit-test with two sequential claims where second must fail while lease held (ArrayTableGateway can simulate with locking flag).

findings.title: Rate limiting is process-local InMemoryRateLimiter only

locations.snippet: Pure in-memory rate limiter for unit tests (no Redis / Laravel facade).

findings.current_state: Config enables rate_limits (60/min defaults) but makeRegistry only applies config numbers; the limiter concrete remains InMemoryRateLimiter. Contracts/RateLimiter.php notes production may wrap Laravel's RateLimiter, but no binding exists.
findings.recommended_state: Bind a LaravelRateLimiter adapter (Cache/Redis) from config when rate_limits.enabled; keep InMemory only for unit tests. Document that multi-worker hosts must use shared store.
findings.rationale: Agent turn budgets and per-capability limits are security-relevant for runaway tool loops (D-008 related). Process-local counters give a false sense of protection under FPM/queue scale-out.
findings.implementation_hint: Implement Support/LaravelCacheRateLimiter using Illuminate\Cache\RateLimiter; bind in ServiceProvider from rate_limits.driver; unit-test via fake Cache store interface.

findings.title: Idempotency defaults to memory while approvals default database

locations.snippet:
'idempotency' => [
        'enabled' => true,
        // Package default is memory; host apps may rebind a database driver.
        'driver' => $env('CAPABILITIES_IDEMPOTENCY_DRIVER', 'memory'),

findings.current_state: Published defaults: approval.store=database (needs connection + migrations) and idempotency.driver=memory. Comments acknowledge host must rebind, but mismatch means multi-worker mutating invokes re-run despite Idempotency-Key while approvals may persist.
findings.recommended_state: Align production defaults: both database when package is used beyond unit tests, or both memory with loud docs/health warning when memory is active under non-local env. Surface driver status in catalog health.
findings.rationale: D-005 requires durable outcomes for mutating invokes. Default memory store silently fails that guarantee in any multi-process deploy while approval durability suggests production orientation.
findings.implementation_hint: Default CAPABILITIES_IDEMPOTENCY_DRIVER to database when approval store is database; or BootGuard warning when APP_ENV=production and driver=memory.

findings.title: CI only splits packages; no package test/coverage gate
findings.current_state: Only split-packages.yml exists under .github/workflows. Local composer scripts run Pest unit suites; phpunit.xml has no coverage threshold despite AGENTS.md ≥95% blocking policy. phpstan is require-dev without neon or CI job.
findings.recommended_state: Add a unit-test workflow (composer test + go test, coverage report with fail under 95%) on PR/main, before or blocking split. Add phpstan.neon.dist and a static-analysis job. Keep unit-only (no Feature).
findings.rationale: Package repos are mirrored on every main push; without CI gates, broken unit contracts can ship to public package remotes. Project policy already declares coverage as blocking — tooling does not enforce it.
findings.implementation_hint: Workflow: setup-php with pcov, composer test:core/messaging, pest --coverage --min=95; go test -cover ./... in capabilities-cli.

findings.title: CoverageGreen boost suites risk gaming the 95% floor

locations.snippet: REQ-016: exercise remaining uncovered unit paths so package line coverage ≥95%.

findings.current_state: Four large CoverageBoost* files (~2.2k lines) exist specifically to raise line coverage. AGENTS.md forbids gaming coverage with weak asserts or shipping dead code for %.
findings.recommended_state: Fold high-value asserts into domain-named suites (pipeline, HTTP, approval); delete pure line-chasing cases; prefer mutation-resistant asserts. Keep coverage ≥95% via real scenarios from requirements-inventory.
findings.rationale: Line coverage with bulk boost files can mask untested behaviour while satisfying the numeric gate, undermining the monorepo's 'tests define the product' contract.
findings.implementation_hint: Run pest --coverage and inventory which boost cases only touch getters; migrate residual paths into existing Unit/* matrices with behavioural expects.

findings.title: Auth HTTP routes share sanctum middleware with token issuance

locations.snippet: public const PROTECTED includes ROUTE_AUTH_TOKEN and ROUTE_AUTH_DEVICE

findings.current_state: All capability routes share one middleware list from surfaces.http.middleware. Auth token/device/oauth callback routes are also listed in HttpAuthGate::PROTECTED requiring authenticated presentation.
findings.recommended_state: Per-route middleware: public or guest middleware for token/device/oauth callback (with CSRF/state where needed); auth:sanctum for list/describe/invoke/approvals. Gate should not treat auth issuance as already-authenticated.
findings.rationale: CLI/device OAuth cannot bootstrap if issuance endpoints require the token they issue. Homogeneous middleware is a structural block for D-009 CLI client flows.
findings.implementation_hint: Extend RouteTable route defs with middleware_override; HttpRouteRegistrar merges group + per-route middleware.

findings.title: ApprovalPolicy any_staff treats every non-system user as staff
findings.current_state: When policy is any_staff and no staffChecker is injected, every non-SystemActor is treated as staff (tenant match still applies). custom without checker also falls through to actorIsStaff.
findings.recommended_state: Default deny when staffChecker missing; require host to bind staffChecker or use is_staff/roles. Keep permissive behaviour only behind explicit testing helper.
findings.rationale: Hosts selecting any_staff from config without wiring staffChecker get silent open approval within tenant — contrary to multi-tenant safe defaults celebrated elsewhere in the same class.
findings.implementation_hint: return false when no checker and no is_staff; unit test any_staff without checker denies ordinary user.

notes: Monorepo of Laravel packages + Go CLI (not a full Laravel app). Adapted scan plan to packages/laravel-capabilities and packages/laravel-capabilities-messaging (src/config/routes/database/tests sample). Respect AGENTS.md: unit tests only, no Feature/DB test recommendations; messaging must stay out of core; one registry run() path is well-enforced in architecture unit suites. Positive observations: CallerDeriver rejects header-alone upgrades; ApprovalController blocks SystemActor; Telegram webhook secret uses hash_equals; QueryTableGateway refuses silent Array fallback; core migrations have sensible indexes/unique keys; capability authorize callables are honored when present. Do not treat CoverageGreen as proof of behavioural completeness. Go CLI only flagged where PHP package HTTP auth stubs affect the client.
